module_title: Basics of Gravitation: 'G' vs 'g' and Mass vs. Weight
introduction: Gravitation is the weakest but most far-reaching fundamental force in the universe. It is the invisible force that holds us to the Earth and keeps the planets orbiting the Sun.

core_concepts.title: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
core_concepts.description:
The force of attraction between any two bodies in the universe is directly proportional to the product of their masses ($m_1, m_2$) and inversely proportional to the square of the distance ($r$) between them. 
Formula: $F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$

core_concepts.title: Universal Gravitational Constant (G)
core_concepts.description:
It is a constant whose value remains exactly the 'SAME' everywhere in the universe (whether you are underwater or deep in space). 
Value: $G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \text{ Nm}^2/\text{kg}^2$. (Its value was first measured experimentally by Henry Cavendish).

core_concepts.title: Acceleration Due to Gravity (g)
core_concepts.description:
The uniform acceleration produced in a freely falling body due to the gravitational pull of the Earth is called 'g'. 
Its average value on the surface of the Earth is $9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$.

core_concepts.title: Mass vs. Weight
core_concepts.description:
1. Mass ($m$): The amount of matter contained in a body. It 'NEVER changes', no matter where you go in the universe. Unit: kg. 
2. Weight ($W$): The downward force with which the Earth pulls an object towards its center. $W = m \times g$. Since 'g' varies from planet to planet, 'Weight also varies'. Unit: Newton (N).

important_entities.name: Weight on the Moon
important_entities.significance: The gravitational pull of the Moon is about $1/6$th that of the Earth. If your weight is 60 Newtons on Earth, it will be only 10 Newtons on the Moon (but your MASS remains exactly the same).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'What is the difference between G and g?' Remember, Capital $G$ is a 'Universal Constant' (Scalar quantity) that never changes. Small $g$ is 'Acceleration' (Vector quantity) that changes with altitude, depth, and location.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Mass stays the same everywhere. Weight 'wanders' (changes) depending on where you are.

exam_strategy_tips: A direct question in SSC exams: 'What is the SI unit of the Universal Gravitational Constant (G)?' Answer: $\text{Nm}^2/\text{kg}^2$.
